q: Which Meta campaigns are wasting money?

checks.what: tool: uses spend plus an outcome metric

answer:
Short answer: Over the last 7 complete days (2026-10-09 to 2026-10-15, P&L / order-date), several Meta campaigns spent material ad budget while returning well under break-even — they look like money-losers now. Biggest offenders by spend and low net ROAS: TH-012-SNUGBOO — ₹18,002, ROAS 0.7x; TH-336-PAWTECH — ₹16,351, ROAS 1.0x (borderline); TH-383-SUSPENDER-29SEP — ₹12,442, ROAS 0.6x; TH-383-SUSPENDER-26SEP-ADV+ — ₹11,537, ROAS 0.6x; DOG DAD T-SHIRT-CS-06OCT — ₹9,769, ROAS 0.2x; DOG SHOES-10OCT-CS — ₹9,506, ROAS 0.2x.

What’s behind it (top movers):
- High spend, low return: TH-012-SNUGBOO spent ₹18,002 (2026-10-09..15) but net ROAS ≈0.7x — it’s spending at a clear loss.  
- Several product-focused campaigns (DOG DAD T-SHIRT, DOG SHOES) show very low ROAS (~0.2x) on ~₹9–10k spends each — these are high-impact waste.  
- A cluster of “SUSPENDER” campaigns together spent ~₹35–40k across variants but ROAS mostly ~0.55–0.65x — the family is underperforming.  
- Many small campaigns show ROAS = 0 or null (no attributed contribution) — these may be misattributed, untracked, or truly non-performing.

Worth checking: pause or cut budget for campaigns with ROAS <0.5 and >₹5k spend (the DOG and SUSPENDER lines), and run a quick drilldown by adset/creative for TH-012-SNUGBOO to see if one creative or audience is causing most of the loss.

Period: 2026-10-09..2026-10-15 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-15
